genZNote: Colonizes damaged heart valves after a dental cleaning — the classic viridans-strep endocarditis story.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human oral cavity, particularly dental plaque and tooth surfaces
habitat.hostAssociation: An early colonizer of dental plaque; contributes to biofilm formation alongside S. mutans

culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe; grows better with added CO2
culture.hemolysis: Alpha-hemolytic or non-hemolytic (viridans group), variable by strain

biochemicalTests.result: Resistant (distinguishes viridans strep from S. pneumoniae)

identificationClues: Gram-positive coccus in chains, catalase negative
Alpha-hemolytic or non-hemolytic on blood agar — part of the viridans streptococcus group
Optochin resistant and bile-insoluble, distinguishing it from Streptococcus pneumoniae

diseases: Subacute bacterial endocarditis — classic association following dental procedures causing transient bacteremia in patients with pre-existing valvular damage
virulenceFactors: Dextran/glucan production contributing to plaque biofilm
Ability to bind fibrin-platelet matrices on damaged heart valves, facilitating endocarditis
clinicalImportance.transmission: Transient bacteremia following dental procedures or even routine tooth brushing in patients with poor oral hygiene
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A classic cause of subacute bacterial endocarditis in patients with underlying valvular heart disease or prosthetic valves; antibiotic prophylaxis before certain dental procedures is targeted at viridans streptococci including this species
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Blood cultures showing alpha-hemolytic, optochin-resistant streptococci in a patient with new murmur/fever should raise suspicion for infective endocarditis

examFacts.importantDisease: Subacute bacterial endocarditis — classic association following dental procedures causing transient bacteremia in patients with pre-existing valvular damage
examFacts.importantTest: Optochin resistance and bile insolubility distinguish viridans strep from S. pneumoniae
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: The classic viridans streptococcus linked to subacute bacterial endocarditis after dental procedures in patients with damaged or prosthetic heart valves
